state.human: User wants controls for saved Given/When/Then generated code/assets, choose a CLI coding tool and model now (Codex, Muse Code, Claude Code, OpenCode), possible API adapter later, asks root configuration versus in .can, retry/refine and direct JS/CSS access for the agent writing .can files. No generation engine/config schema/adapters are implemented.

verified.existing_design: Shared .can-owned identity, prompts, typed contracts, explicit generation/preparation, zero-AI ordinary builds, persisted actual generator identity and finite retry/reset/accept. Runtime implementations/server rendering target workerd; client interactions target browser. Inline and named Then style and frontend default are human requirements.
verified.repo: No generation root config API exists. DESIGN forbids authored app/source/dependency/interface manifests but derives those from .can; a tooling configuration for how AI generation executes is new scope motivated by the user, not duplicated business composition.
verified.cli: Executable paths found for codex, claude, opencode and muse. Installed codex exec and Muse exec help expose noninteractive/model/JSONL; Claude help exposes print/model/output formats. Official Codex/Claude/OpenCode docs confirm automation/model controls. OpenCode local help cannot open its outside-workspace log, so adapter runtime/auth is not qualified. Muse help emits a failed update-marker write warning but prints command controls. No provider inference, login or generation run was made.
verified.files: Current app generated extensions do not exist. Existing proposal recommends saved bytes/artifact paths and separate candidates; stable inline identity and JS interface/permission integration are concrete open implementation gaps.

state.equal_outcomes: Compare all candidates as unimplemented designs. Every candidate must support concise .can authoring, explicit effective CLI/model identity, no AI every build, clean-checkout rebuild from saved code, direct developer/authoring-agent refinement, truthful origin metadata, current permissions/contracts/workerd checks, no lost edits, finite failure/retry/unknown-outcome handling and stale late-result refusal. No choice proves arbitrary JS semantics or grants new authority. Avoid implementation/proof frameworks not needed for this outcome.

config_owner.instructions: Compare project root profiles, source recipes and external user/command preferences for selecting the coding tool/model. Recommend the best shared and portable control surface under the same required outcomes.

criteria.root_profiles: Put CLI/model/bounded execution preferences in a shared root generation-tool config, with frontend/backend logical defaults and optional named source or per-run profile overrides. Source owns prompts/contracts. Credentials stay in CLI-native login or local environment. A new small tool config is needed; it must not become an app/dependency registry.
criteria.source_recipes: Put effective CLI/model recipe selection in .can owning declarations, reusable via local recipe definitions and implicit defaults. Credentials stay CLI-native/environment; local tool path overrides remain machine preferences. Selection is visible with source intent, but execution preferences enter the language and can increase source coupling/authoring.
criteria.external_preferences: Keep provider/model choice in user tool preferences or generation command flags only, persisting effective selection with saved output. Source stays small and teams can use different tools, but shared project defaults require recorded conventions or replay of the saved selected recipe.
criteria.open: Keep config ownership open if the same portability/identity/direct-authoring outcomes are not sufficiently defined.

file_owner.instructions: For AI-generated implementation that authors can refine directly, where should the current code live: editable primary files, immutable accepted artifacts or a base-plus-patches composition? Weigh simplicity against the same compatibility/concurrency guarantees.

criteria.editable_primary: Track generated JS/CSS and minimal source association metadata as directly editable primary implementation files. Normal build reads current bytes and validates compatibility without AI or mandatory candidate ceremony for ordinary edits. Generation/refine write separate candidates, accepted only if captured source/contracts and current file bytes still match. Record original generated bytes historically; mark later edits without falsely attributing their author. Needs drift detection and finite compatibility refresh for manual source changes.
criteria.immutable_primary: Keep accepted generated implementation immutable; direct authoring-agent edits are placed into editable candidates and promoted after checks. Clean checkout contains accepted bytes and tools expose candidate paths. This gives an explicit replacement boundary but every direct refinement needs promotion; immutability does not prove semantics.
criteria.patch_overlay: Track a generated base plus editable manual/agent patches; normal build applies the saved patches without AI, and refinement/regeneration produce a candidate composition. Origin and patch metadata are distinct. This retains replayable refinements but adds a second authored implementation/reconstruction layer and conflict handling after base changes.
criteria.open: Keep file ownership open if source association/compatibility requirements prevent choosing a complete minimal workflow now.
